title: stage masks: matte ink
shortDescription: The Inkwell Séance: a horror title card turns into the level through ink blots that grow by the progress of the transition — matte() in 'coverage' mode, a living mask stage, a slider that holds any frame
description:
A `StageDirector` with the stack `[title card, wet edge]`. The title card of *The Drowned House* — a nitrate photograph of a gothic house standing in a flooded marsh, fog drifting over it, chrome art-deco letters, grain and flicker — turns into the level: the hallway on its ground floor, the water up to the knees, a lantern wading through it that nobody carries, and four portraits whose eyes follow the lantern (or your pointer). It turns back the same way.

The change is `director.replace(title, hall, {effect: inkIn, duration, easing})` with `inkIn = matte({mask: ink})` in its default **`'coverage'` mode**: the picture of the mask stage *is* the transition — its alpha is the share of `to` at every pixel. The mask stage `ink` is a `Stage2D` that is never in the stack; the director joins it only while the transition runs. Seven blots grow from their seeds, push out tendrils and melt into each other until they cover the screen: a TSL metaball field whose radii grow by **`ink.progressNode`**, the eased progress as a uniform, and fifty-six drops that splash ahead of the blots, sized on the CPU by **`ink.progress`**. Neither looks at the clock, so the ink follows the transition whatever its duration or easing — pick `ease-in` and a long duration, and the blots creep at first and rush at the end: compare *time / duration* with *ink.progress*. `matte()` holds both ends itself: 0 at progress 0, everything at progress 1.

*scrub by hand* (key S) starts the transition with `manual: true`, and the slider writes `transition.progress`: the blots hold still at any frame, because they grow by the progress and nothing else. *wet edge* is a layer above the slot, not part of the matte: it draws the same blots from the same uniforms, black-violet and glossy, so the ink is seen where the title gives way — switch it off to see the bare matte. See [Stage masks: a transition through a living matte](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/stages.md#a-transition-through-a-living-matte).
